title: Your first song in LibreTracks, on mobile

scenes.text: Hi. In this video you'll build your first song in LibreTracks on your phone or tablet, and play it live. All you need are the song's stems on the phone: one audio file per instrument.
First, create a session. Press Create, type its name, and press Create again. A session is your setlist: it can hold a single song, or the whole Sunday set.
Now press Add audio, and the phone's file picker opens. This phone is in Spanish, but the steps are the same: tap Audio, press and hold the first file, choose select all in the menu, and confirm.
LibreTracks asks whether you want to put them on the timeline: press OK. The song is created, with each audio file on its own track.
The song gets a generic name. Tap its bar, up on the ruler: its actions appear at the bottom. Press Rename Song, and type its name.
Right there, Song key sets its key. It shows next to the name, and in Live View.
Tap the tempo, at the top left, and type the song's BPM. Turn on the click with the note button, and press play: the click has to land right with the drums.

To keep your tracks tidy, group them into folders. Tap a track, press the select several button, and tap the other one. Then, Move to folder, New folder, and give it a name. Its volume, mute and solo affect all of its tracks.
Now the markers. Tap the ruler to move the cursor, and in the bar at the bottom press Section: intro, verse, chorus. They're for jumping live. With Cue you add directions for the band, like all in.
With the markers in place, turn on the voice guide, with the megaphone button. Listen: before each section, a voice announces it, and counts it in.
And now, play. This is Live View: each section is a big button. Tap it, and the song jumps to that part at just the right moment.
Save the session, and you're done. The complete guide, button by button, is at libretracks dot com. Enjoy playing!
